cause:
I traced picks made the way the test makes them: CDP tracing plus the V8 sampler on a source-map build of 00e6a4c, 360x800, processor slowed four times, load 0.5 to 1.5. Thread time equals wall time in these tasks, and the same work varies about 2x between picks, so any task of about 25 ms or more can pass 50 ms.

E6, node 1: each of the seven 27x27 grids (E, F, H, the two relation sides, the move, the signed move) was written, parsed and drawn in one task of 20 to 61 ms. Parsing alone took 10 to 22 ms. The first grid (E) took 35 to 62 ms, including a minor GC of 6 to 10 ms. These grids were the long tasks the observer saw; once it was the Board mount instead.

Other steps at 21 to 56 ms:
- orbit panel with its layout: 23 to 56
- the task that loads the state, including the pickers' options: 21 to 46
- take-down of the old panels: 21 to 39
- board resolution plus default node: 22 to 36
- the two tables of the table view: 25 to 29

E7 untraced at base, 30 picks: the long tasks were the Board mount (75, 66), take-down (51), the load step (57) and the orbit panel (66, 53).

After my change, every remaining E7 long task I could identify (3 of 40 picks at the CI base) is the mount of the string viewer's shared Board. That is one Svelte component mount (Board, seven Node, Roads with six roads, seven buttons): 21 to 60 ms in 50 traced picks (median 32), with no GC in it. About half the time is in Node.svelte, a quarter in Roads.svelte and a sixth in the buttons. When two Boards have already been mounted on the page it takes at most 26 ms, so the cost comes from cold code. T12 cannot split a single component mount. Drawing the string panel first gave a median of 25 against 27 ms over 20 picks each, which is within noise, so I did not keep it.

The 170 ms task (14b log) started at 1315, within a few ms of the pick. The only task that runs then is the change event: Playwright's selectOption (its injected script is about 60% of the samples), T12's pickBoard and the building line. That task normally takes 20 to 43 ms (median 27 over 41 traced tasks). The rerun used 2 workers, and the other worker was loading tool pages at that moment. With a second browser loading pages here, the same task took 20 to 31 ms. So 170 ms was contention, and I could not reproduce it at load 2 or less. Its partner of 53 ms at about +420 ms falls where the base draws the orbit panel and the first grid, the two heaviest E6 steps.
before: 00e6a4c, T12.spec.ts long-task tests --repeat-each 40 --workers 1: root load 1.15-1.45: E6 37/40, E7 38/40 (long tasks 50-59 ms). CI base /mutation_game/ load 1.06-1.34: E6 37/40, E7 40/40 (51-53 ms).
after: c326dd3 (same code at 68d93ef): root load 0.83-1.47: E6 40/40, E7 39/40 (one task of 60 ms). CI base load 1.30-1.46: E6 39/40 (60 ms), E7 38/40 (56, 59 ms). E7 at the CI base misses the target of at most 1 failure in 40. The attribution batch puts every remaining E7 long task on the shared Board's mount.
handoff:
Only T12's own files changed (T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte, t12/OrbitLayers.svelte, t12/rep.ts, math/MatrixView.svelte), plus one new e2e test and one new unit test in T12's files.

MatrixView's props are unchanged. It now also exports matrixTableParts, matrixInput, adoptableTable and ADOPT_CELLS; matrixTable's output is identical. OrbitLayers also exports orbitSvgLayers, and orbitSvg's output is identical. representationDimension is now cached per representation.

After a pick:
- each grid is built outside the page about 250 cells per task, and its MatrixView takes it over only when its props match
- the orbit's layout gets a task of its own, and its SVG layers are written when shown
- the board is resolved in a task of its own
- the state and tool are made a task before they load
- the pickers show the target one task early
- the previous panels are taken down in two tasks
- the orbit table is drawn 20 rows per task

The final DOM is unchanged; only the transitional drawing order differs.

E6 meets the target. E7 does not at the CI base, because the shared Board's mount is a single task of 21 to 60 ms that T12 cannot split. The owner needs to choose one of:
(a) the Board's owner lightens its mount (Roads uses spread attributes; each button has six listeners).
(b) T12 keeps one Board across picks and updates its props. A2 to E7 would then create 5 of 7 nodes, an estimated 20 to 30% saving, but the old board would show while a pick builds, which is a visible change.
(c) Accept the residual. I did not change the test, its threshold or its throttling.
